symbols.name: \(T\)
symbols.def: Number of treatment decisions in each complete trajectory.

symbols.name: \(c\)
symbols.def: Known strength of the globally stable longitudinal odds shift.

symbols.name: \(X_t\)
symbols.def: Observed binary covariate immediately before action \(A_t\).

symbols.name: \(Y^{\bar a_T}\)
symbols.def: Potential terminal outcome under action regime \(\bar a_T\).

symbols.name: \(P\)
symbols.space: probability laws for the observed trajectory and all potential terminal outcomes
symbols.def: A law whose observed margin is the distribution of \(O\).

symbols.name: \(P^n\)
symbols.def: The \(n\)-fold product of the observed margin of \(P\).

symbols.name: \(\pi_t^P\)
symbols.def: A version of the conditional probability of action one under \(P\).

symbols.name: \(d_t^P\)
symbols.def: Conditional normalizing factor for the odds-multiplier action law.

symbols.name: \(Q_{P,c}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the space of \(O\)

symbols.name: \(h_t(z)\)
symbols.def: The realization of \(H_t\) contained in leaf \(z\).

symbols.name: \(m_h(P)\)
symbols.def: Probability under \(P\) of the binary prefix \(h\).

symbols.name: \(m_{h1}(P)\)
symbols.def: Probability under \(P\) of prefix \(h\) followed by action one.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\psi\)
symbols.space: measurable maps from the sample to \([0,1]\)
symbols.def: Generic possibly randomized point estimator based on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\).

symbols.name: \(I\)
symbols.def: Generic possibly randomized interval based on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\).

symbols.name: \(k\)
symbols.def: Number of early periods used to create paired contexts.

symbols.name: \(b_{r_0}(\eta)\)
symbols.def: Increment in the tie-randomized majority mean when \(r_0\) fair bits are shifted to success probability \(\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\eta)\).

symbols.name: \(r(n,T,c)\)
symbols.def: A generic candidate comparison scale for \(R(n,T,c)\).

symbols.name: \(\ell(n,T,c)\)
symbols.def: A generic candidate comparison scale for \(L(n,T,c)\).

symbols.name: \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{tree}}\)
symbols.space: finite multiscale procedures on compatible binary trees

symbols.name: \(a_0\)
symbols.def: A universal numerical constant independent of \(n,T,c\).

symbols.name: \(A_0\)
symbols.def: A universal numerical constant independent of \(n,T,c\).

assumptions.condition: The observed trajectories \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) have joint law \(P^n\).
The terminal outcome satisfies \(Y\in[0,1]\) almost surely.
For every \(\bar a_T\in\mathcal A^T\), \(Y=Y^{\bar a_T}\) on the event \((A_1,\ldots,A_T)=\bar a_T\) almost surely.
For every \(t\in[T]\) and \(\bar a_T\in\mathcal A^T\), \(A_t\perp Y^{\bar a_T}\mid H_t\) under \(P\).
The rule \(\widehat\psi\) is a measurable, possibly independently randomized map of \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\) into \([0,1]\).
The rule \(I\) is a measurable, possibly independently randomized connected subinterval of \([0,1]\) satisfying \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_T}P^n\{\psi_T(P,c)\in I\}\geq0.95\).

definitions.name: Unrestricted complete-history class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_T=\{P: P\text{ is a full-data law at horizon }T\text{ satisfying }\mathrm{ass:binary\text{-}covariates},\ \mathrm{ass:binary\text{-}actions},\ \mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}outcome},\ \mathrm{ass:consistency},\text{ and }\mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}exchangeability}\}\).

definitions.name: Globally stable incremental action kernel
definitions.construction: For every \(t\in[T]\) and history \(h\), set \(q_t^P(1\mid h)=\delta\pi_t^P(h)/d_t^P(h)\) and \(q_t^P(0\mid h)=\{1-\pi_t^P(h)\}/d_t^P(h)\), where \(d_t^P(h)=1+(\delta-1)\pi_t^P(h)\).

definitions.name: Incrementally intervened trajectory law
definitions.construction: Construct \(Q_{P,c}\) by replacing, in the sequential factorization of the observed margin of \(P\), every action kernel \(P(A_t\in\cdot\mid H_t)\) by \(q_t^P(\cdot\mid H_t)\) and retaining every covariate and outcome kernel.

definitions.name: Total finite-tree identifying functional
definitions.construction: Define \(F_{T,c}(P)=\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z_T}s_z(P)\delta^{\sum_{t=1}^T a_t}\prod_{t=1}^T m_{h_t(z)}(P)/\{m_{h_t(z)}(P)+(\delta-1)m_{h_t(z)1}(P)\}\), with each ratio set to one when its prefix mass is zero.

definitions.name: All measurable point estimators
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,T}=\{\widehat\psi:\widehat\psi\text{ is a measurable, possibly independently randomized map of }(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\text{ into }[0,1]\}\).

definitions.name: Uniformly honest connected intervals
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_{n,T,c}=\{I:I\text{ is a measurable, possibly independently randomized connected subinterval of }[0,1]\text{ and }\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_T}P^n\{\psi_T(P,c)\in I\}\geq0.95\}\).

definitions.name: Known-propensity oracle experiment
definitions.construction: Define \(R^{\mathrm{or}}(n,T,c)\) and \(L^{\mathrm{or}}(n,T,c)\) by the formulas in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risk}\) and \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}length}\), respectively, after adjoining \(\Pi(P)\) to every observation available to the decision rule.

definitions.name: Complement-paired context experiment
definitions.construction: For \(1\leq k<T\) and \(r_0=T-k\), let the first \(k\) covariates and actions be independent fair bits, pair the resulting \(4^k\) contexts by flipping only \(X_1\), set all later covariates to zero, and let \(f_{r_0}(b)=\mathbf 1\{\sum_jb_j>r_0/2\}+\frac12\mathbf 1\{\sum_jb_j=r_0/2\}\). Under \(P_0^{k,r_0}\), the late actions are independent fair bits and \(Y=f_{r_0}(A_{k+1},\ldots,A_T)\). Under each \(P_B^{k,r_0}\), assign to the two contexts in every pair a fixed late string and its bitwise complement, and use the corresponding deterministic outcome. Define \(\overline P_1^{(n,k,r_0)}\) by averaging \((P_B^{k,r_0})^n\) over independent uniform pair strings.

definitions.name: Compatible-prefix approximation and testing handle
definitions.construction: Starting from the centered functional \(G_{T,c}\), partition unconditional subtree-root masses into dyadic occupancy ranges, approximate each rational descendant contribution by a polynomial in unconditional child masses subject to the parent-sum identities, lift monomials by multinomial factorial moments or degenerate \(U\)-statistics with covariance retained for nested prefixes, and construct dual moment-matched priors by drawing whole legal subtrees rather than independent prefix counts.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_T\), \(Q_{P,c}\ll P\) on the observed trajectory space, conditional versions on \(P\)-null histories do not affect the target, and the causal incremental terminal mean is identified by \(\psi_T(P,c)=E_P[YW_T^P]=F_{T,c}(P)\).
statements.justification: This proposition fixes the exact support-respecting observed-data functional before any minimax analysis.
statements.gap: KimKennedyNaimi2021, Theorem 3.1, gives longitudinal identification with dropout; the present complete-data finite-tree formula makes null-prefix compatibility explicit for the unrestricted binary experiment.
statements.consumer: The estimator and converse can operate on unconditional leaf and prefix masses without imposing treatment positivity.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_T\), \(E_P[W_T^P]=1\), \(E_P[(W_T^P)^2]\leq\cosh(\eta/2)^{2T}\leq\exp(c^2/4)\), and \(|\psi_T(P,c)-\mu(P)|\leq B(c)\leq c/3\).
statements.justification: The dimension-free second moment separates stable oracle weighting from the possible cost of learning an unrestricted history tree.
statements.gap: KimKennedyNaimi2021, Theorem 6.1, studies a constant-propensity variance ratio; this bound is uniform over every history-dependent propensity tree and every deterministic action node.
statements.consumer: The natural sample mean and its bias-aware interval give total fallback procedures for every \(n,T,c\).

statements.statement: There exist universal constants \(a_0,A_0\) such that, for every \(n,T\geq1\) and \(c\in[0,1]\), \(a_0/n\leq R^{\mathrm{or}}(n,T,c)\leq A_0/n\) and \(a_0/\sqrt n\leq L^{\mathrm{or}}(n,T,c)\leq A_0/\sqrt n\). The upper procedures are clipped inverse-likelihood weighting and its Chebyshev interval, and the lower bounds use a Bernoulli terminal-outcome subexperiment.
statements.justification: A uniform parametric oracle benchmark makes any unknown-history penalty an information effect rather than exploding intervention weights.
statements.gap: KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies compares local efficiency bounds under structured policy models; it does not give this all-sample unrestricted-history oracle decision bound.
statements.consumer: The oracle comparison tells longitudinal analysts whether supplying a fitted propensity tree could change the order of attainable precision.

statements.statement: At every interior finite-tree law, the full-law canonical gradient is \(D_{P,c}=YW_T^P-\psi_T(P,c)-\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{\delta-1}{d_t^P(H_t)}E_P[YW_T^P\mid H_t](A_t-\pi_t^P(H_t))\). Its centered counterpart satisfies \(\lVert D_{G,P,c}\rVert_{L_2(P)}\leq2c\), while \(\lVert D_{P,c}\rVert_{L_2(P)}<3\), uniformly in \(T\); the bounds extend to boundary laws through finite-simplex continuity.
statements.justification: The result exhibits a bounded local efficiency problem even where the global finite-sample experiment can be hard.
statements.gap: KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies derives the extra score-projection term for natural policies under Markov structure; the present formula retains the entire unrestricted history and quantifies exact cancellation as \(c\to0\).
statements.consumer: Semiparametric users can distinguish a valid fixed-law efficiency calculation from a uniform guarantee over sparse histories.

statements.statement: The sequential target is not a one-normalizer static exponential tilt on \(\mathcal P_T\): at \(T=2\), with constant covariates, fair \(A_1\), deterministic \(A_2=A_1\), \(Y=A_2\), and \(c=\sqrt2\log(3/2)\), the sequential functional equals \(3/5\), whereas tilting the observed law once by \(\delta^{A_1+A_2}\) and globally normalizing yields \(9/13\).
statements.justification: The counterexample blocks a tempting flattening that would erase the nested-prefix learning problem.
statements.gap: SchindlShenKennedy2024 and HuangDongLinAntonelli2026 analyze static single-normalizer tilts; their target algebra cannot be substituted for the sequential functional.
statements.consumer: The lower-bound and estimator proofs must preserve the original longitudinal intervention rather than import a static rate verbatim.

statements.statement: For the construction in \(\mathrm{def:paired\text{-}witness}\), every fixed \(P_B^{k,r_0}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_T\) and satisfies \(\psi_T(P_B^{k,r_0},c)=1/2\), whereas \(\psi_T(P_0^{k,r_0},c)=1/2+b_{r_0}(\eta)\) with \(b_{r_0}(\eta)\geq c\sqrt{r_0/T}/16\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{TV}((P_0^{k,r_0})^n,\overline P_1^{(n,k,r_0)})\leq\rho_{n,k}\). At \(k=1,r_0=2,n=2\), the mixture total variation is exactly \(3/8\), shifted partner masses cancel, and the functional differs from a static tilt.
statements.justification: This is the required destructive audit of the sparse-history lower mechanism before it is used in a frontier theorem.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete uses within-category collisions for a one-time treatment functional; complement-paired whole subtrees and exact sequential target cancellation are different proof objects.
statements.consumer: The witness supplies all-estimator and all-randomized-interval converses without assuming concentration of a random target.

statements.statement: There exist universal constants \(0<a_0\leq A_0<\infty\) such that, whenever \(T\geq2k_n\), \(a_0\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\}\leq R(n,T,c)\leq A_0\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\}\) and \(a_0\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}\leq L(n,T,c)\leq A_0\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}\). The upper estimator is the clipped natural sample mean, the interval adds the deterministic radius \(B(c)\) to a Hoeffding radius, and the lower bounds range over every measurable estimator and every possibly randomized honest connected interval.
statements.justification: The theorem establishes a substantive non-oracle penalty in a solved regime and pins its exact shrinking-strength transition.
statements.gap: KimKennedyNaimi2021 gives a special constant-propensity variance comparison, and MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022 gives a one-stage fixed-target oracle gap; neither proves this unrestricted sequential long-history result.
statements.consumer: Many-visit incremental-intervention workflows obtain a rigorous warning that stable oracle weights need not imply uniform root-\(n\) estimation when histories are learned.

statements.statement: At \(c=0\), \(q_t^P=\pi_t^P\), \(Q_{P,0}=P\) on observed trajectories, and \(\psi_T(P,0)=\mu(P)\); uniformly for every \(n,T\geq1\), \(R(n,T,0)\asymp n^{-1}\) and \(L(n,T,0)\asymp n^{-1/2}\). For each fixed \(T\), the finite-tree empirical plug-in estimator also has risk of order \(n^{-1}\), with a comparison constant allowed to depend on \(T\).
statements.justification: The exact zero-shift reduction is the non-negotiable sanity check for every proposed transition formula.
statements.gap: Kennedy2019JASA supplies the fixed-horizon incremental functional; the uniform \(c=0\) decision reduction records the boundary that a growing-tree approximation must preserve exactly.
statements.consumer: Any software implementation can test its correction algebra by verifying exact collapse to the ordinary sample mean at zero shift.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{tree}}\), construct and characterize the optimal finite-order approximation of \(G_{T,c}(P)\) over every compatible collection of nested prefix masses, with a matching second-moment bound for its multinomial factorial statistic and a dual pair of legal subtree priors. Determine the first mixed-prefix correction beyond scalar low-count polynomial approximation and prove that the approximation, variance, and testing scales coincide uniformly in \(n,T,c\), including null prefixes and saturation.
statements.justification: This is the exact intermediate-history theorem missing between the fixed-alphabet and birthday-collision endpoints.
statements.gap: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 and MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022 lift scalar cell polynomials by independent Poisson factorial moments; nested longitudinal prefix counts obey parent-sum constraints and the target weights depend on those same masses.
statements.consumer: A solution supplies the bias and variance certificate needed by a total minimax estimator and a shortest honest interval.

statements.statement: Exhibit explicit evaluable functions \(r(n,T,c)\) and \(\ell(n,T,c)\), a total finite-data estimator \(\widehat\psi^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}\), and a total connected interval \(I^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}\) such that, for universal \(0<a_0\leq A_0<\infty\) and every \(n,T\geq1\), \(c\in[0,1]\), \(a_0r(n,T,c)\leq R(n,T,c)\leq\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_T}E_{P^n}[(\widehat\psi^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}-\psi_T(P,c))^2]\leq A_0r(n,T,c)\) and \(a_0\ell(n,T,c)\leq L(n,T,c)\leq\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_T}E_{P^n}[\operatorname{length}(I^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c})]\leq A_0\ell(n,T,c)\). Require \(I^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}\in\mathcal C_{n,T,c}\), state finite computational cost, include every logarithmic transition and saturation factor, and derive from these functions necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform consistency along every \(T=T_n,c=c_n\) and necessary and sufficient conditions for \(R/R^{\mathrm{or}}\) or \(L/L^{\mathrm{or}}\) to diverge in order.
statements.justification: This question is the theorem-level kernel: one matched all-sample phase diagram jointly governs estimation, honest inference, consistency, and the value of propensity knowledge.
statements.gap: No inspected result, including KimKennedyNaimi2021, KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies, MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022, or ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete, gives an unrestricted nested-prefix frontier for a propensity-dependent target.
statements.consumer: The EAGeR-style long-history workflow and the \(\texttt{imtp}\) implementation obtain a theorem stating when sample size must grow with history complexity despite bounded oracle weights.

sampling_model.design: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent complete trajectories with common observed law equal to the observed margin of \(P\in\mathcal P_T\).
sampling_model.units: Each trajectory contains \(T\) binary covariates, \(T\) binary actions, and one terminal outcome in \([0,1]\).
sampling_model.treatment: At time \(t\), the unknown propensity \(\pi_t^P(H_t)\) may depend arbitrarily on the full observed past; deterministic actions and null histories are permitted.
sampling_model.overlap: No positive lower bound is imposed on \(\pi_t^P(H_t)\) or \(1-\pi_t^P(H_t)\); domination follows from the incremental kernel itself.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The analyst receives only \(n,T,c\), the alphabets, and the trajectories. The handle uses occupancy-adaptive polynomials of unconditional compatible prefix masses and nested-count factorial corrections; the oracle benchmark additionally supplies \(\Pi(P)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.1 gives fixed-horizon nuisance-rate inference, while Theorem 6.1 compares incremental and deterministic inverse-weighting variances under a common constant propensity.
The paper derives and attains local efficiency bounds for behavior-dependent tilting and modified-treatment policies under Markov or non-Markov policy models.
The paper proves sharp finite-sample known-versus-unknown behavior-policy bounds for one-stage fixed-target bandit evaluation and uses Chebyshev approximation in a low-exploration regime.
Theorems 2 and 4 derive high-dimensional discrete-covariate lower bounds for one-time treatment-specific and homogeneous-effect functionals using moment matching and collisions.
Theorem 2 lower-bounds estimation error for a continuous-exposure static exponential-tilt estimand as the tilt grows.
The paper derives efficiency, minimax, and finite-tilt normality results for a multivariate static exposure tilt with one conditional normalizer.
Theorem 2 gives a parametric fixed-policy bias-variance expansion showing that longer-history behavior estimation reduces asymptotic variance while increasing finite-sample bias.
CoinDICE constructs behavior-agnostic policy-value intervals from embedded Markov occupancy equations and proves asymptotic and nonasymptotic coverage statements.

tldr: Longitudinal incremental interventions retain bounded oracle likelihood-ratio variance when the per-period log-odds shift is \(c/\sqrt T\), but this local stability need not control the global cost of learning an unrestricted exponentially branching propensity tree. The proposal first proves exact finite-tree identification, a dimension-free local efficiency bound, and a complement-paired sparse-history theorem giving \(R(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\}\) and \(L(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}\) once \(T\) exceeds a birthday-collision threshold. Its open kernel is a compatible-prefix polynomial approximation and testing duality that must close the entire intermediate regime, yielding explicit all-sample risk and honest-length functions, total algorithms, every logarithmic transition, exact consistency conditions, and the phase diagram for when knowing the complete propensity tree changes the order of precision.

project_justification.gap: Kim, Kennedy, and Naimi derive identification, efficient influence functions, and nuisance-controlled fixed-horizon inference, but their growing-horizon theorem is a constant-propensity variance comparison. Natural-policy efficiency theory remains local, while bandit and high-dimensional discrete minimax results flatten the data into unrelated one-stage cells and do not contain endogenous products of compatible prefix ratios.
project_justification.niche: The centered finite-tree functional has a dimension-free local gradient yet can separate under mixtures that are indistinguishable until contexts collide. This creates an unstudied intermediate regime in which approximation error, nested-count covariance, and legal-subtree testing affinity must be solved together.
project_justification.fill: The paper isolates the first mixed-prefix correction, constructs an occupancy-adaptive polynomial or factorial estimator on the original trajectory experiment, calibrates a bias-aware honest connected interval, proves matching all-procedure converses, and evaluates the resulting finite optimization into explicit functions of \(n,T,c\).

related_work: Kim, Kennedy, and Naimi, \cite{KimKennedyNaimi2021}, Introduction, Theorems 3.1, 4.1, 5.1, and 6.1, and the concluding discussion, supply the writing model: long histories and positivity motivate incremental interventions, after which identification and fixed-horizon efficiency lead to a many-timepoint precision question. Their Theorem 6.1 assumes a common constant propensity for a variance ratio and does not optimize risk over unrestricted history trees. Kennedy, \cite{Kennedy2019JASA}, gives the underlying support-respecting binary incremental functional and fixed-horizon efficiency theory. Kallus and Uehara, \cite{KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies}, Definitions 1--2, Theorems 2 and 8--11, Algorithm 1, and the proofs in Sections 7--8, show how behavior dependence adds a score term to the influence function; their global horizon conclusions rely on policy-model structure and do not imply finite-sample uniform estimation over all histories. Ma, Zhu, Jiao, and Wainwright, \cite{MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022}, Introduction, Theorems 1--3, the Chebyshev construction near equation (64), and its proof, provide the closest switching, low-count polynomial, and behavior-mixture machinery, but their target policy is fixed and arms are not nested. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015}, Introduction, the smooth--nonsmooth estimator construction, Lemma 4, Theorems 2--4, and the approximation--moment lower-bound section, supply the factorial-moment lift that the prefix recursion must adapt. Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, \cite{ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete}, Introduction, Theorems 2 and 4, their fuzzy-hypothesis proofs, and Discussion, show that unseen discrete contexts and within-cell collisions create causal minimax penalties; their one-time weighted means omit sequential parent-sum compatibility. Schindl, Shen, and Kennedy, \cite{SchindlShenKennedy2024}, Theorem 2 and its Le Cam proof, and Huang, Dong, Lin, and Antonelli, \cite{HuangDongLinAntonelli2026}, Theorem 4 and the efficiency appendix, establish tilt-sensitive static continuous-exposure theory; \(\mathrm{prop:static\text{-}nonreduction}\) shows why those single-normalizer results do not flatten the present target. Zhou, Hanna, Zhu, Yang, and Shi, \cite{ZhouHannaZhuYangShi2025}, Introduction, Theorem 2 and its projection proof, and the concluding discussion, characterize a parametric fixed-policy history-length bias-variance tradeoff rather than an unrestricted minimax frontier. Liu, Bacon, and Brunskill, \cite{LiuBaconBrunskill2020}, Theorem 1, conditional Monte Carlo derivation, and Discussion, motivate prefix conditioning but establish only sufficient variance comparisons. Cai and Low, \cite{CaiLow2004}, Theorem 1, Section 2 construction, and Discussion, provide the ordered-modulus logic for expected length; CoinDICE, \cite{DaiEtAl2020CoinDICE}, Theorems 1--3 and the interval optimization, instead depends on Markov occupancy equations absent here. Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart, \cite{RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2016TR}, provide higher-order influence-function and degenerate-\(U\)-statistic machinery under complexity-reducing projections, whereas the present open step must build the projection from raw prefix occupancy.
technical_internal_limitation: The proved-regime targets recorded here do not identify the intermediate frontier. A dyadic approximation bound without a nested-count second-moment theorem is insufficient, and independent Poisson prefix counts are incompatible with parent-sum identities. The exact all-sample rate may differ from each currently available envelope, so neither \(4^T/n\), a sole birthday threshold, nor \(L\asymp\sqrt R\) is asserted. The \(k=1,r_0=2\) enumeration and finite-difference influence checks are diagnostics, not proofs.
honest_scope: Identification is given, and the binary completely observed experiment is deliberately narrower than the EAGeR dropout analysis. The long-history theorem, zero-shift reduction, oracle benchmark, and local-gradient bound are concrete claims to prove. The compatible-prefix approximation and the full matched phase diagram remain first-class open questions. No Markov, smoothness, sparsity, positive-propensity floor, or supplied nuisance kernel is introduced. At \(c=0\) the target and both optimal rates reduce exactly to ordinary bounded-mean estimation. The proposal does not turn its rates into a numerical sample-size prescription for richer covariates or dropout.

seed_details.seed: Sharp all-sample minimax risk and honest-length frontier for the unrestricted longitudinal incremental mean
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:1907.04004, Introduction, identification Theorem 3.1 and its g-formula construction, efficient influence-function Theorem 4.1 and Appendix F, growing-horizon Theorem 6.1 and Appendix F.3, and the concluding discussion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the constant-propensity variance calculation in Theorem 6.1 by a finite-tree decision problem; the first new step is a compatible approximation theorem for the centered rational prefix functional, not an influence-function expansion.
seed_details.destination_search: Exact searches for longitudinal incremental minimax history-tree learning and propensity-dependent prefix polynomial estimation found fixed-horizon incremental theory, static continuous tilts, structured natural-policy efficiency, and one-stage discrete or bandit minimax results, but no full target theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from KimKennedyNaimi2021 because the incremental weight has a uniformly bounded second moment under \(c/\sqrt T\).
seed_details.rebuttal: A bounded oracle weight controls estimation when the propensity tree is supplied; the complement-paired mixture gives a global unknown-law penalty while the full-law influence-function norm remains bounded.

seed_details.seed: Compatible-prefix polynomial and factorial estimator for the intermediate-history regime
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:2101.07781, Introduction, known- and unknown-policy Theorems 1--3, switch-estimator convex program, Chebyshev construction around equation (64), its low-count bias-variance proof, and the concluding proof section.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the per-arm Poisson unbiased-moment identity by a recursion on unconditional child masses whose factorial statistics share descendants and therefore require a nested covariance theorem.
seed_details.destination_search: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015, RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2016TR, and ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete provide adjacent polynomial, higher-order, and causal collision threads; none treats a target weight made from the same compatible prefix probabilities being estimated.
seed_details.red_team: A direct tensor product of one-dimensional Chebyshev polynomials and factorial moments solves every node independently.
seed_details.rebuttal: Prefix counts are sums of common leaf counts, child errors propagate through later normalizers, and independent nodewise approximation violates both parent-sum compatibility and the needed variance accounting.

seed_details.seed: Exact oracle-information phase diagram for behavior-dependent longitudinal policies
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:2006.03886, Introduction, Definitions 1--2, tilting-policy Theorem 2, non-Markov Theorems 8--11, Algorithm 1, nuisance remainder analysis, and the proof of the efficiency-bound comparison.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the tangent-space comparison of supplied and estimated behavior policies by a finite-experiment comparison in which the target itself changes with every unknown prefix propensity.
seed_details.destination_search: MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022 supplies a one-stage oracle gap, HiranoImbensRidder2003 supplies the opposite estimated-score efficiency phenomenon, and ZhouHannaZhuYangShi2025 supplies a parametric history-length bias-variance decomposition; no source gives necessary and sufficient order separation for the present endogenous sequential policy.
seed_details.red_team: The oracle gap is already determined by the larger natural-policy efficiency bound in KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies.
seed_details.rebuttal: Both local efficiency bounds can be uniformly bounded while global minimax risk separates, so a tangent-space variance ratio does not determine the sparse-history phase boundary.

seed_details.seed: Shortest finite-sample honest connected interval by trajectory-mixture modulus inversion
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:math/0503662, Introduction, Theorem 1 lower bound, Section 2 interval construction, and Section 2.3 discussion of expected-length adaptation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the Gaussian ordered modulus of a linear functional over convex classes by an iid trajectory-mixture modulus for a nonlinear finite-tree functional, then separately exploit interval connectedness to transfer two coverage events.
seed_details.destination_search: KimKennedyNaimi2021 gives asymptotic nuisance-controlled intervals, DaiEtAl2020CoinDICE gives Markov estimating-equation intervals, and Armstrong--Kolesar bias-aware theory assumes smooth regression classes; none minimizes expected connected length over the unrestricted trajectory simplex.
seed_details.red_team: The optimal interval length is automatically the square root of minimax mean-squared risk.
seed_details.rebuttal: That conversion is false without a confidence procedure and a coverage-specific converse; sparse mixtures can affect expected length through testing affinity differently from squared loss.

seed_details.seed: Adaptive retained-prefix-depth oracle inequality with endogenous-target correction
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:1910.06508, Introduction, conditional Monte Carlo representation, Theorem 1 and proof, finite- and infinite-horizon comparisons, and Discussion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Derive an exact identity for conditioning the propensity-dependent likelihood ratio on a shorter prefix; unlike fixed-policy conditional importance sampling, this creates a mixed-prefix target correction before any Lepski selection.
seed_details.destination_search: Jiang--Li sequential doubly robust recursion, Kallus--Uehara marginalized ratios, and ZhouHannaZhuYangShi2025 history-dependent propensity fitting all retain Markov, parametric, or fixed-policy structure and provide no unrestricted depth oracle inequality.
seed_details.red_team: Rao--Blackwellization guarantees that a shorter retained history always improves risk.
seed_details.rebuttal: Conditioning reduces variance for a fixed unbiased target, but here shortening history alters an unknown behavior-dependent intervention and introduces bias whose first mixed-prefix term is not a conditional-variance identity.

seed_details.seed: Global-to-local efficiency breakdown radius around sparse propensity trees
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:2006.03886, Introduction, tilting-policy efficient influence function, efficiency-bound comparison, non-Markov embedding, and estimator remainder proof.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After deriving the bounded full-tree canonical gradient, replace ordinary local asymptotic normality by a growing-alphabet neighborhood modulus that locates the largest radius on which regular root-\(n\) estimation remains uniform.
seed_details.destination_search: SchindlShenKennedy2024 supplies tilt-calibrated Le Cam alternatives and ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete supplies growing-category fuzzy hypotheses, but neither derives a local-neighborhood radius for a nested natural policy.
seed_details.red_team: This merely restates that pointwise semiparametric efficiency need not imply uniform minimaxity.
seed_details.rebuttal: An explicit critical neighborhood radius and a two-sided local minimax theorem would be a new quantitative object, but it is less directly responsive than the requested all-sample frontier.

seed_details.seed: Shrinking-strength onset boundary between the natural mean and the sparse-history penalty
seed_details.anchor: Prior proposal on the stationary partially observed overlap frontier, open-ended question on shrinking overlap
seed_details.anchor_opened: Prior-proposal core at the cited open-ended question and its honest-scope boundary; the iid complete-trajectory destination was then checked against Kennedy2019JASA and SchindlShenKennedy2024.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the dependent observed-filter likelihood calculation by iid complementary-prefix mixture affinity while preserving exact cancellation at \(c=0\).
seed_details.destination_search: Kennedy2019JASA gives the exact local target expansion, SchindlShenKennedy2024 gives static tilt-dependent testing, and the paired witness gives the long-history endpoint; the intermediate onset remains unoccupied.
seed_details.red_team: A Taylor expansion around \(c=0\) immediately gives the transition.
seed_details.rebuttal: The product \(T\eta\) can diverge, unseen-prefix errors are nonuniform, and the zero-shift cancellation must survive the approximation statistic rather than only the population expansion.

seed_details.seed: Transition limit law for an occupancy-adaptive prefix estimator
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:2505.22492, Introduction, Theorem 2, projection-based proof, extensions to sequential and doubly robust estimators, and closing discussion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace their fixed-dimensional parametric Taylor expansion by a triangular-array Hoeffding decomposition for a data-dependent-order factorial statistic at the occupancy transition.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found Gaussian fixed-horizon efficient limits and Poissonized large-alphabet risk bounds, but no stable candidate normalization or unique limiting experiment for this unrestricted all-sequence transition.
seed_details.red_team: A central limit theorem is secondary until the rate and estimator are known.
seed_details.rebuttal: A non-Gaussian transition law could be valuable, but the current substrate does not identify one normalization uniformly over arbitrary \(T_n,c_n\), so this lane has no credible first-version survivor.

seed_details.seed: Data-driven choice of incremental strength with minimax welfare regret
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:1907.04004, Introduction, incremental-effect curve definition, uniform-in-strength inference theorem, EAGeR analysis, and conclusion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Promote \(c\) from a known intervention index to a decision selected from the estimated effect curve and lower-bound regret relative to the best incremental shift.
seed_details.destination_search: Policy-learning searches found empirical welfare maximization for externally indexed policy classes, not behavior-dependent policy curves whose value changes with an unrestricted unknown history tree.
seed_details.red_team: This changes the scientific target from estimating a prespecified intervention to optimizing a policy without any intervention-cost or welfare criterion in the topic.
seed_details.rebuttal: A defensible regret theorem would require an added utility or cost primitive, so it is a scope expansion and is not retained for this proposal.

seed_details.seed: Permutation or conformal inversion for a nonlinear incremental distribution functional
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:math/0503662, Introduction, ordered-modulus lower theorem, interval construction, and discussion; targeted symmetry and conformal searches were then run for off-policy values.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Find a finite group action under which a null value of \(F_{T,c}(P)\) is invariant while the nuisance trajectory law remains unrestricted.
seed_details.destination_search: No exchangeability orbit was found that fixes the nonlinear propensity-dependent null across arbitrary trajectory laws; existing conformal counterfactual methods require placebo or time symmetry absent from iid trajectory sampling.
seed_details.red_team: There is no exact symmetry to invert beyond exchangeability of the sample labels, which carries no information about a nonlinear distribution functional.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds on the unrestricted class, so this lane is dropped rather than relabeled as an asymptotic interval problem.

literature_map: Selected full-frontier thread: KimKennedyNaimi2021 supplies the exact longitudinal incremental setup, positivity motivation, fixed-horizon identifying and influence-function constructions, and its special constant-propensity growing-horizon comparison. KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies establishes the closest local efficiency analysis for behavior-dependent policies; MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022 establishes the closest finite-sample oracle-information separation; ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete establishes the closest causal unseen-context converse; SchindlShenKennedy2024 and HuangDongLinAntonelli2026 cover static tilt-sensitive minimax and limit theory. None subsumes the nested sequential target, and the explicit \(T=2\) law rules out a one-normalizer reduction. Selected approximation-engine thread: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 gives smooth--nonsmooth polynomial estimation and approximation--moment duality, MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022 adapts Chebyshev polynomials to unknown logging, RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2016TR provides higher-order degenerate-\(U\)-statistic corrections, and ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete provides causal fuzzy-hypothesis constructions. Their first common failure is that they treat unrelated cells or fixed-dimensional projection kernels, whereas a legal trajectory subtree imposes nested parent-sum constraints. Honest-length thread: CaiLow2004 gives ordered-modulus expected-length lower bounds, KimKennedyNaimi2021 gives asymptotic nuisance-controlled incremental intervals, DaiEtAl2020CoinDICE gives behavior-agnostic intervals from Markov occupancy equations, and Armstrong--Kolesar bias-aware inference balances explicit bias against stochastic radius on smooth regression classes. No closer source gives minimax expected connected length for the unrestricted nonlinear trajectory functional. The M11 limit-law lane was searched through ZhouHannaZhuYangShi2025 and large-alphabet transition theory but lacked a stable normalization before the rate is known. The M16 policy-regret lane required a new welfare criterion, and the M17 symmetry lane lacked a nuisance-invariant group action; both were dropped rather than padded.
novelty_justification: The closest causal paper proves identification and fixed-horizon efficiency and asks a many-timepoint precision question only through a constant-propensity variance ratio. The closest natural-policy paper compares local efficiency bounds under structured policy models. The closest finite-sample minimax papers treat one-stage fixed targets or one-time discrete adjustment. The selected kernel instead asks for one explicit all-\(n,T,c\) frontier for an endogenous sequential intervention over every compatible binary history tree, jointly matching point risk and honest connected-interval length and characterizing the exact value of knowing the full propensity tree. Its non-verbatim content is certified by the static-tilt counterexample and by the first mixed-prefix obstruction: factorial contributions share descendant counts and must obey parent-sum identities. The long-history paired-mixture theorem and the bounded centered influence function provide direct evidence that the problem is neither a routine oracle variance calculation nor a generic unseen-cell restatement.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic:
Sharp unknown-history minimax frontier for globally stable longitudinal incremental interventions. For all integers n>=1,T>=1 and known c in [0,1], observe n iid complete trajectories O=(X1,A1,...,XT,AT,Y), all Xt and At binary and Y in [0,1]. Let Ht=(X1,A1,...,X_(t-1),A_(t-1),Xt). The law class P_T includes every trajectory law on this sample space, with arbitrary history-dependent covariate, action and outcome kernels. For causal interpretation impose consistency and sequential exchangeability (no hidden treatment confounding); no missingness, Markov, smoothness, sparsity or positive treatment-probability floor is imposed. The data analyst knows n,T,c and the alphabet, and is not supplied any true kernel. Define pi_t(Ht)=P(At=1|Ht), eta=c/sqrt(T), delta=exp(eta), and q_t(P)(1|Ht)=delta*pi_t/[1+(delta-1)*pi_t]. Replace all action kernels by q_t(P), retaining covariate/outcome kernels. Let psi_T(P,c) be the resulting terminal mean. This intervened law is dominated by P, so conditional versions on P-null histories do not change psi. Deterministic treatment and null histories are included. Determine explicit evaluable functions r(n,T,c) and ell(n,T,c), up to universal multiplicative constants independent of n,T,c, for R(n,T,c)=inf_{all measurable estimators} sup_{P in P_T} E_P[(hatpsi-psi_T(P,c))^2] and L(n,T,c)=inf_{I} sup_{P in P_T} E_P[length(I)], where I is a measurable connected interval in [0,1], with optional independent randomization, satisfying inf_{P in P_T} P_P(psi_T(P,c) in I)>=0.95. Prove matching upper and lower bounds uniformly for every n,T,c, including saturation, shrinking c, and all logarithmic transition factors. Upper results must supply total finite-data algorithms for an estimator and such an interval, with stated computational cost; converses range over all estimators/intervals on the original iid experiment and the same P_T. Derive necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform consistency along sequences T=T_n,c=c_n and characterize exactly when knowing the complete propensity tree changes the order of risk or honest length. At c=0 recover R of order 1/n and L of order 1/sqrt(n). The known-propensity benchmark is uniformly order 1/n and 1/sqrt(n) for all T,c in the domain. Whether or where unknown propensities create a strict penalty is answer-open, not assumed. Exact rates, transitions, estimator algebra and proof mechanics are outputs. A fixed-T EIF, oracle-only bound, unmatched rate bracket, or illustrative impossibility example does not satisfy the kernel. Consumer: Kim, Kennedy and Naimi, Incremental Intervention Effects in Studies with Dropout and Many Timepoints (2021), analyze EAGeR aspirin adherence and pregnancy across many weeks; the mtpverse/imtp software implements incremental interventions with learned treatment propensities. The theorem would establish whether increasing the history length requires more subjects or structural restrictions even when the oracle weights have bounded second moment, informing how these workflows justify estimation precision for long histories. This binary, completely observed experiment is an explicitly restricted theoretical benchmark, not a numerical sample-size prescription for their richer covariate/dropout analysis. Sources https://arxiv.org/pdf/1907.04004 and https://github.com/mtpverse/imtp . PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A bounded presolve derived more than the known-propensity variance calculation. Complement-paired context priors make every deterministic-history intervention mean exactly one-half, while randomized late actions shift a majority outcome. Their observed-data mixtures agree whenever sampled contexts occupy different pairs, producing a sparse-history lower mechanism without random-target concentration. A natural-mean estimator with an explicit deterministic intervention-bias envelope supplies a matching long-history upper route. The full-law influence function also has a dimension-independent second-moment bound, separating local efficiency from uniform sparse-history difficulty. Independent finite enumeration checked the paired-target identity, nonuniform early intervention weights, and small-mixture likelihoods; finite differences checked the influence formula. These checks are not proofs of uniform bounds or the full frontier. Deterministic actions, null histories, zero and shrinking intervention strength, and recent static incremental/OPE comparators were considered.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Close the sharp intermediate-history transition through a compatible prefix-probability approximation/variance theorem and matching all-procedure converse, including connected honest-interval length; endpoint results must not replace this requirement.
EARLY KILL TEST: Audit the k=1,r=2 paired model and two-action prefix functional: verify mixture indistinguishability, shifted pair cancellation, and nonidentity with a static tilt, then identify the first mixed-prefix correction absent from prior theorems. Stop and re-gate if the witness fails or an existing exact reduction supplies the entire frontier.
